questions: Does the 12 mm footprint recover the iteration 3 oval result (max_error near or under 0.06, progress near 0.87), or does oval progress drop, which would mean the 16 mm footprint was helping?
Do the s-bend and slalom max_error values move below 0.0615 and 0.0611, or stay at the 0.06 off-track limit? If they stay, the bend exit is limited by turn authority or speed, not by sensing.
Does line_loss_events stay at or below 1.0 per run on every track? A rise above 1.0 would mean the 12 mm footprints are missing the tape edge on tight bends.
Does steering_oscillation on the oval move from 0.339, and does control_effort change? If the footprint change alone lowers oscillation, the sensing gain was the cause and not the controller.

intent: Revert the outer pair to ±0.04 m (dropping the ±0.05 widening that lowered oval progress and did not fix the bend exits) and test sensor_size 0.012 at y = 0.06, holding every other value at the iteration 3 best design. This is a single-variable test against the 203.20 best: the footprint size is the only change.
learning: Iteration 4 showed that widening the outer pair to ±0.05 m does not help bend exits (s-bend and slalom max_error rose) and reduces oval progress, so outer spacing is not the lever at this sensor row. The forward row at y = 0.06 is what improved the oval. Next, test whether footprint size, rather than spacing, limits the bend-exit response. If the 12 mm footprint does not change the s-bend or slalom exit, the next geometry step is wheel_track 0.085 m for more turn authority, with the controller carrying oscillation.
rationale: Iteration 4 scored 187.24, below the iteration 3 best of 203.20. Widening the outer pair to ±0.05 m moved oval max_error back up to 0.0607 (from 0.0598) and cut oval progress from 0.87 to 0.80. It did not fix the bend exits: s-bend max_error rose to 0.0621 and slalom to 0.0627, with progress falling to 0.13 and 0.10. The outer-sensor spacing is therefore not the bend-entry lever. Oval line_loss_events fell to 0.5, but the other tracks stayed at 1.0, so line loss is not the constraint either. The forward row at y = 0.06 is the geometry change that clearly helped (oval max_error under 0.06 and progress up from 0.53 to 0.87), so I keep it. I revert the outer pair to ±0.04 m, which was the best-scoring spacing. I also make one geometry change that has not been tested: sensor_size 0.012 (12 mm) instead of 16 mm. This tests the Integrator's requested change 1 in its intended form, with the spacing held at ±0.04 m. Iteration 0 showed that 12 mm footprints gave weak near-centre signal, so the change is a real trade-off and not a sure gain. Body_length 0.22, wheel_track 0.09, wheel_radius 0.03, body_width 0.12 and mass 0.5 stay as in iteration 3, so the only change from the best design is the footprint size. Expected result: a score near 203 if the footprint is neutral, or a s-bend/slalom max_error improvement if smaller footprints react more sharply at the bend exit. If line_loss rises above 1.0 on any track, the 12 mm footprints are not helping and I will return to 16 mm.
